# `price-rule` commands

## `price-rule activate`

Make an inactive price rule price new lines again.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Feature | — |

## `price-rule create`

Add a price rule, as the anchor's Advanced Pricing does: a sales line whose item, customer, class, rep, date and quantity meet its conditions defaults to the rule price. Conditions, all of which must hold (an empty list matches all): items (a parent item covers its subitems), item_categories, customers (a customer covers its jobs), customer_types, classes (the line's, else the sale's), sales_reps, the transaction date from date_from through date_to, and min_quantity in the item base unit. The adjustment starts from the item sales price (basis sales_price) or its cost (basis cost), moves it down (a discount) or up (a markup) by a percent (kind percent) or an amount per base unit (kind amount), given as value, or as quantity breaks (breaks: [{min_quantity, value}], below the first the rule does not apply), never below zero, and rounds it: cent, x.99 or x.95 (up to the next price ending so) or dollar. priority orders rules (1 first; default after every rule). When a price level and rules, or several rules, price one line, the company preference (`price-rule set-preferences`) picks the lowest price (the default) or the first rule by priority. The rule a line used is captured on it, so later edits never change saved documents. Example: 10% off pipe fittings for Acme through December.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | price-level |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/price-rule.create` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow price-rule create --name "Riverside clearing 10% off" --customers "Riverside Apartments" --items "Mainline Clearing" --value 10 --date-to 2026-12-31 --reason "Year-end deal" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "price-rule create", "input": {"name": "Riverside clearing 10% off", "customers": ["Riverside Apartments"], "items": ["Mainline Clearing"], "value": "10", "date_to": "2026-12-31"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | `--description` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `priority` | `--priority` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Order among rules, 1 first. Defaults to after every rule there is. |
| `items` | `--items` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Items the rule prices; a parent item covers its subitems. Item, customer, class or rep IDs or names; an empty list (the default) matches every one. |
| `item_categories` | `--item-categories` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Item categories the rule prices, with their subcategories. |
| `customers` | `--customers` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Customers the rule prices for; a customer covers its jobs. |
| `customer_types` | `--customer-types` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Customer types the rule prices for, with their subtypes. |
| `classes` | `--classes` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Classes of the line (or the sale) the rule applies to, with their subclasses. |
| `sales_reps` | `--sales-reps` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Sales reps of the sale the rule applies to. |
| `date_from` | `--date-from` | string \| null | no | yes | null | First transaction date the rule applies to. |
| `date_to` | `--date-to` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Last transaction date the rule applies to. |
| `min_quantity` | `--min-quantity` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Smallest line quantity, in the item base unit, the rule applies to. |
| `kind` | `--kind` | literal["percent", "amount"] \| null | no | yes | null | percent (of the basis) or amount (per base unit). Default percent. |
| `direction` | `--direction` | literal["down", "up"] \| null | no | yes | null | down (a discount, the default) or up (a markup). |
| `basis` | `--basis` | literal["sales_price", "cost"] \| null | no | yes | null | sales_price (the item price, the default) or cost (the item cost). |
| `value` | `--value` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The percent, such as 10, or the amount, such as 1.50. Give value or breaks. |
| `breaks[].min_quantity` | inside `--breaks` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Smallest quantity, in the item base unit, this break applies from, such as 10.; minimum length 1; maximum length 32 |
| `breaks[].value` | inside `--breaks` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | The percent or amount for quantities from min_quantity up to the next break.; minimum length 1; maximum length 32 |
| `rounding` | `--rounding` | literal["cent", "x.99", "x.95", "dollar"] \| null | no | yes | null | cent (the default), x.99 or x.95 (up to the next price ending so), or dollar (nearest whole unit). |
| `name` | `--name` | string | yes | no | — | Rule name, unique, such as "Acme fittings 10% off".; minimum length 1; maximum length 200 |

## `price-rule deactivate`

Stop a price rule pricing new lines (a promotion that has ended early); it is kept, and documents that used it keep their prices.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `price-rule set-preferences`

Set how a line chooses among its price level and matching price rules: lowest_price (the lowest wins; a tie goes to the price level, then the first rule by priority) or priority (the first matching rule by priority wins, over the price level). Saved documents keep their prices.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | price-level |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/price-rule.set-preferences` |

## `price-rule update`

Change a price rule using its expected version; name only what changes (a condition list given replaces that list; an empty list matches all). Saved documents keep the rule as they captured it; new lines and re-priced lines use the change.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | price-level |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/price-rule.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow price-rule update "Riverside clearing 10% off" --expected-version 1 --rounding x.99 --reason "Charm pricing" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "price-rule update", "input": {"rule": "Riverside clearing 10% off", "expected_version": 1, "rounding": "x.99"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | `--description` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `priority` | `--priority` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Order among rules, 1 first. Defaults to after every rule there is. |
| `items` | `--items` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Items the rule prices; a parent item covers its subitems. Item, customer, class or rep IDs or names; an empty list (the default) matches every one. |
| `item_categories` | `--item-categories` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Item categories the rule prices, with their subcategories. |
| `customers` | `--customers` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Customers the rule prices for; a customer covers its jobs. |
| `customer_types` | `--customer-types` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Customer types the rule prices for, with their subtypes. |
| `classes` | `--classes` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Classes of the line (or the sale) the rule applies to, with their subclasses. |
| `sales_reps` | `--sales-reps` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Sales reps of the sale the rule applies to. |
| `date_from` | `--date-from` | string \| null | no | yes | null | First transaction date the rule applies to. |
| `date_to` | `--date-to` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Last transaction date the rule applies to. |
| `min_quantity` | `--min-quantity` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Smallest line quantity, in the item base unit, the rule applies to. |
| `kind` | `--kind` | literal["percent", "amount"] \| null | no | yes | null | percent (of the basis) or amount (per base unit). Default percent. |
| `direction` | `--direction` | literal["down", "up"] \| null | no | yes | null | down (a discount, the default) or up (a markup). |
| `basis` | `--basis` | literal["sales_price", "cost"] \| null | no | yes | null | sales_price (the item price, the default) or cost (the item cost). |
| `value` | `--value` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The percent, such as 10, or the amount, such as 1.50. Give value or breaks. |
| `breaks[].min_quantity` | inside `--breaks` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | Smallest quantity, in the item base unit, this break applies from, such as 10.; minimum length 1; maximum length 32 |
| `breaks[].value` | inside `--breaks` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | The percent or amount for quantities from min_quantity up to the next break.; minimum length 1; maximum length 32 |
| `rounding` | `--rounding` | literal["cent", "x.99", "x.95", "dollar"] \| null | no | yes | null | cent (the default), x.99 or x.95 (up to the next price ending so), or dollar (nearest whole unit). |
| `rule` | `RULE` | string | yes | no | — | Price rule ID or name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `name` | `--name` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |

| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.
